summary: The truncation note hardcoded into every "truncated" finding's detail asserts a specific causal mechanism ("reshaped by a source line wrap") that the code does not actually verify — `checkQuote`'s "truncated" branch only checks whether the citation matches after generic whitespace normalization and comment-marker stripping (`joinedProse`/`normalizeWhitespace`), which will also fire for a quote that merely strips a leading `//`/`#` on a single line, or one whose only difference from the diff is internal whitespace (multiple spaces or a tab) with no newline crossed at all. In those cases the finding is stamped with a claim about a mechanism ("a source line wrap the diff breaks with a real newline") that never happened, misrepresenting to a reader why the citation was accepted.

evidence.text: 'Evidence citation confirmed genuine, reshaped by a source line wrap the diff breaks with a real newline — not invented.';
